 O R D E R

Dated this the 19th day of November, 2019 Vide the impugned proceedings dated 22.4.2019 in CC No.469/2017, the learned Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court, Kakkanad dismissed the complaint under Section 256 of the Cr.PC stating that the complainant has never appeared before the court,
while accused 1, 2 and 6 applied and A4 was not represented.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court, Kakkanad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is true that the case was posted for hearing the complaint.
But the observation of the learned Magistrate that the complainant has never appeared, does not appear to be true from the copy of the proceedings, which is produced before this Court.
It is seen that he has appeared on many dates, including on 5.10.2018.
From 23.3.2019, the complainant was absent and thereafter, the case was posted for hearing on three dates and he could not appear.
However, there should have been a representation for the complainant.

There is no The Food Safety Officer vs Basil P.Mathew on 19 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170858173/
2 doubt about that.

entities.text: Food Safety Officer vs Basil P.Mathew on 19 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Considering the fact that an offence under the Food Safety and Standards Act,
2006 is a serious offence, the accused cannot be left off merely for the absence of the complainant.

Hence, the proceedings dated 22.4.2019 is set aside and the case is restored to the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court, Kakkanad with a direction that hereinafter, the complainant shall be present on all postings without fail and also shall be represented by the Prosecutor.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The Criminal LP is disposed of.
